# agent/secret-exfiltration

Secrets sent over the network.

A command that reads a secret source (`.env*`, `~/.aws`, `~/.ssh`, `printenv`, `env`, `gh auth token`, keychain tools) and sends it to the network (`curl`, `wget`, `nc`, `scp`, `ssh`, `gh gist create`) in the same command line, through a pipe, a substitution, or a file argument.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: Denied. Keys passed in a request header (curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ...") are how APIs authenticate and are not reported.
- Looks at: agent actions in hooks: commands, file reads, and prompts.
- References: [CWE-200](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/200.html), [CWE-201](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/201.html), OWASP ASI02, OWASP LLM02.

## Why it matters

This is the shape of a prompt injection that steals credentials: read the keys, send them to a server. A key sent this way cannot be recalled and has to be rotated.

## How to fix

Do not send secrets over the network; if a service needs a key, the user should configure it there.

## If the check is wrong

This check runs in agent hooks. Allow a command prefix with `commands.allow` in `ubon.json`, or set `"rules": { "agent/secret-exfiltration": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).
